Szamosszeg Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Szamosszeg, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews reportedly settled in Szamosszeg at the end of the 18th century; population grew from 20 (1840) to 96 by 1880, holding steady near 94 by 1930. The community maintained its own synagogue, school, and mikveh. Ten men were conscripted for forced labor in 1942; immediately after Passover 1944, following German occupation, residents were sent to the Mátészalka Ghetto and deported to Auschwitz by month's end. Only seven survivors returned, and the community was never re-established. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1853, its newest to 1932.
